Added: **Title fight.** Above the drivers and constructors standings: how many points are left, who can still catch the leader, and what the leader needs to clinch it at the next round — "with a win, Russell 10th or lower". Once it is decided, the card names the champion and the round where the title was won, with a trophy in the team's colour.

**Circuit facts.** An open race card gets a Circuit row with the corners and laps. Tap it for the track map, the circuit type, what a pit stop costs with and without a Safety Car, and who won and took pole there last year.

**Weather for the weekend.** The same circuit sheet has a row for every session starting within a week: the sky at the start, or the risk of rain across the whole session, plus the temperature and the wind. "Drying track" means it rained before the start.
**Share the circuit.** The circuit sheet has a Share button: the track, its corners and laps, and the weekend weather on one card.

**iPhone Duo.** On the outer display, and on the inner one in landscape, the tab bar stands at the side next to the camera, the way the system's does, and Back and Share move there too. Nothing hides under the side status bar.

**Side by side on big screens.** On the open iPhone Duo, an iPad or an open foldable, the schedule shows the race dashboard next to the list, the drivers standings show a season head to head, settings open their pages on the right, and during a session the chat shows live timing beside the room, however you opened it. On iPad the tab bar moves to the top; on a wide Android screen it becomes a side rail.

**Ask Siri when the next race is.** "When is the next race in PlanB?" answers without opening the app. Shortcuts can open the schedule, the standings, the chat, race control or predictions, and Spotlight finds this season's rounds and drivers. iOS only; Siri understands the phrases in English.
**Bring the Live Activity back.** Swiped it off the Lock Screen by accident? During qualifying, a sprint or the race, the live screen shows "Show on Lock Screen" to put it back.
**One stack per race weekend.** On iOS, session reminders and race chat notifications for the same weekend are grouped together in Notification Center.
Changed: **Positions first.** During a session the schedule shows the top three under the track status, with the latest race control message below. The live screen opens on positions; race control is the second tab, and a flag alert still opens it directly.

**Share cards stand out in a chat.** Every card you share now has a blue header cut by a red-and-white kerb, with the city of the race in big slanted type. The race start is the largest thing on a weekend card, the leader of a standings or a result gets their own row ("K. Antonelli"), and the top 10 fits on one card. The rest of the card follows your light or dark theme.

**Predictions open faster.** Pick the podium shows the drivers you already have instead of waiting for the network, and both prediction screens show their shape while they load — the podium is there at once, only the names fill in.

**Race chat keeps up.** Typing no longer slows the room down, the chat loads even before its live connection is up, and after a reconnect it fills in every message you missed. A message that failed to send can be removed, and its text goes back to the message box.
On iOS, countdown digits roll instead of jumping.
A support link pasted into a message opens, with or without `https://`.
Rotating the phone is no longer locked to portrait.
Bottom sheets stay phone-sized and centred on wide screens.
Built on Expo SDK 58 (React Native 0.88).
Fixed: Driver numbers are right again: Norris is 1 and Verstappen 3, not their old permanent numbers.
On iOS, sent messages and quoted replies no longer lose their text, and a reply bubble is as wide as its quote.
After you send a long message, the message box shrinks back to one line.
Choosing "Skip" for notifications during onboarding means it: the app no longer shows the system prompt on the next launch.
Looking at last season in Settings no longer cancels your session reminders.
Retry on the error sheet now actually loads again, and a slow connection gives up after 20 seconds instead of hanging.
A finished race leaves Upcoming on time, even if the app stayed open in the background.
A Live Activity never starts empty when the positions cannot be read, and an old one from the same session is replaced instead of staying beside it.
Widgets draw the track and the rows properly in the tinted and clear Home Screen styles.
Turning the phone no longer leaves the app drawn at the old width with a black band beside it.

Added: **Pick the podium.** During race week, the weekend card asks who will finish first, second and third. Picks close when qualifying starts — on a sprint weekend, the main qualifying on Saturday — and are scored a couple of hours after the race: 3 points for a driver in the right place, 1 for a podium driver in the wrong one, and 2 more for the exact podium. The season table ranks everyone, and the top ten show their place next to their name in race chat.

**Play before you sign in.** You can build a podium straight away; it stays on your phone until you lock it in. Signing in is asked only then, together with what it gives you, and your podium is saved as soon as you are in.

**Compare with the paddock.** Once your podium is locked in, see which drivers everyone else put on each step, and whether your pick was a bold call. It appears once ten people have made their picks for the round.

**Your podium stays with you after picks close.** The podium button on the weekend card turns into your podium — "VER NOR LEC" — and then into your points once the round is scored, on the Past card as well. The weekend card keeps all its actions in one row under the schedule — live chat, the race dashboard, your podium and share — instead of a stack of wide buttons. The pick screen shows the real podium next to yours, and you can share your podium as an image. Predictions open from the Chat tab, where "Your rounds" lists every round you called this season.

**More on Apple Watch.** Three pages to scroll through with the Digital Crown: the next session with a live countdown, the whole weekend, and the top of both championships. The season calendar is one tap away.
**Twelve reactions in race chat.** 🏁 👏 🐐 🤡 💀 🍿 join the six you had, laid out in two rows when you press and hold a message.
**Double-tap a message to react with 🔥.** A second double-tap leaves it in place rather than taking it off.
Changed: **A new first launch.** Five start lights mark the steps and go out together at the end. Each step shows the real app — the next race in your time zone, the race dashboard, the widgets — and one step lets you pick your team, which sets the app's colour. It shows once on updating too, starting from the team colour you already chose.
The Apple Watch widget moves up in the Smart Stack in the last day before a race and while it runs.

**The position chart reads at a glance.** It counts in laps: every lap takes the same width, so the chart lines up with the tyre strategy and the gap chart below it, and each driver's line takes one step per lap instead of every momentary swap, so overtakes show as lines crossing rather than a comb of spikes. The top three are in colour and the rest in grey, with a teammate dashed; the starting order runs down the left and the finishing order down the right. Tap a name on either side to follow that driver, or drag across the chart to see the order on any lap. The zoom buttons and the row of driver chips are gone, and the safety car and VSC are labelled on their bands. The shared card draws it the same way.
**One kind of screen title.** Every screen names itself the same way, in plain case rather than capitals, and buttons no longer shout either.

**The predictions table explains itself.** Before the first round is scored, it shows how points are earned and takes you straight to this round's podium. Picking a podium shows each driver's team, marks empty steps with a dashed outline, and puts the scoring rules above the list instead of after twenty drivers.

**The whole weekend on the medium iPhone widget.** It used to show only qualifying and the race, so on a sprint weekend practice, sprint qualifying and the sprint were missing. It now lays the weekend out day by day in your time zone, dims what is over, marks the next session and counts down to it rather than to the race. Above that: the full race name, the circuit and where it is.

**Unread chat on the app icon.** While a race weekend is on, the PlanB icon shows how many messages in race chat you have not read yet, so you can see the room is busy without opening the app. It clears when you open the chat.

**A reminder before podium picks close.** Picks close when qualifying starts; an hour before that you get a reminder if you have not picked a podium for the round yet. In that last hour the "Pick the podium" button on the weekend card and the lock button count down the minutes, and the card button goes away when picks close. The reminder can be switched off in Settings → Notifications.

**Share the top ten from race control.** The share button there sends the first ten as they stand right now — gaps, intervals, tyres and who is in the pits in a race, best laps and the cut in qualifying — with the track status and the lap or qualifying part. It used to send the last few race control messages.

**The Live Activity starts by itself.** Five minutes before qualifying, a sprint or the race, the session appears on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island without opening the app (iOS 17.2 and later), marked "Starting soon" until the lights go out. It is on by default and can be switched off in Settings → Notifications; the "Follow on Lock Screen" button on race control is gone.

**A clearer menu when you press and hold a message.** The message itself sits on top with its time, then the reactions, then Reply and Mention, with Report and Block below in a quieter list. Reporting now asks what is wrong — spam, harassment, hate speech or something else — before you add any details.

**Replying gets you typing.** Swiping a message, tapping Reply or Mention opens the keyboard straight away, and a reply arrow appears under the message as you swipe. With VoiceOver, Reply and the 🔥 reaction are in the message's actions.

**The track status above race chat looks like what it is.** It sits in its own panel with an arrow, so it is clear that a tap opens race control, and in a race or sprint a thin bar under it fills lap by lap in the colour of the track status. The same panel is at the top of the schedule, where it shrinks to a single line while you scroll the races.
**A half-written message waits for you.** Leave race chat to check the standings and come back: your text and the message you were replying to are still there.
Fixed: **Widgets now move on after the race.** The Next Race widget kept showing `LIVE` all evening after the flag, on iPhone and Android. Three hours after the start it now switches to the next round by itself, without opening the app, and its countdown stays accurate between updates.
The season progress widget colours the round that has just finished as soon as you open the app, instead of waiting a day or more for the result to appear.
On Apple Watch, a finished race no longer shows "Race week" until the end of the week.

**Race dashboard after a delayed start.** At the rain-delayed Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, the position chart sat flat for an hour and a half and then stopped after six laps, so Leclerc, fourth, appeared to finish eighteenth and no safety car was shown. The chart now runs from the real start to the flag, on every race — normal ones had lost their last few minutes too.

**Tyre strategy after a safety-car start.** The strategy chart showed tyre changes that never happened and missed ones that did — Verstappen on softs from lap 2, Piastri with a single lap on hards, Bottas with a stop he never made. Stints now follow the pit stops, and a VSC that turns into a full safety car ends where the safety car begins.
**Qualifying shows Q1, Q2 or Q3 instead of a lap count**, on race control, above the chat and on the Lock Screen. Laps are counted only in a race or a sprint.
In the dark theme the iPhone widgets use a lighter blue for the round number, the countdown and the race time, which were hard to read on black.
Opening race chat during a session flashed a block of race control messages for a moment before the conversation loaded. The room now shows its loading state until the messages are in.
A removed chat message no longer offers Reply or reactions, which the chat turned down anyway.

Added: **Live during the session.** While a session runs, a strip under the race chat header and above the schedule shows the track status — green, yellow, safety car, VSC or red flag. Tapping it opens live race control, and a Standings tab with gaps, intervals, tyres and pit stops.

**The race on your Lock Screen** (iOS 17.2 and later). Qualifying, the sprint or the race in the Dynamic Island and on the Lock Screen: track status, the lap count, the top three with gaps and your team's driver. Tap "Follow on Lock Screen" in race control, or turn on "Live Activity during sessions" in Settings → Notifications to have it start by itself.
**Track status alerts.** An optional push for a safety car, a VSC, a red flag and the return to green, under Settings → Notifications. Off by default.

**Every lap, sector by sector.** Tap a driver in the classification to see each lap split into sectors, coloured the way the broadcast does it, with tyres, pit stops and deleted laps struck through with the reason. The best lap and the ideal lap sit on top and can be shared as a card.
**Head to head in one race.** Pick two drivers to see the gap between them lap by lap, with pit stops and safety car periods, their best sectors and a score.
**Teammate battle.** On a driver's standings card, compare two drivers across the season: qualifying, races, points, wins, podiums and poles, with a dot for every round. Either driver can be swapped.
Changed: Safety cars, red flags, penalties and deleted laps now appear in the race chat right where they happened.
Fixed: The race chat stays open when rain or a red flag pushes the race past its scheduled slot.
The dark theme no longer flashes white while switching screens.
Results that are not published yet read "Update in progress" instead of showing an error.

Added: **Share what you are looking at.** A race weekend, a session result, either championship table and two sections of the race dashboard can each be sent out as a card. Every card carries a link that opens the app at exactly that screen, and a page on the web for anyone who does not have the app. Weekend cards show the circuit and say which time zone the times belong to. The race dashboard sends its classification, with the places each driver gained or lost since the start, or the position chart of the whole race, keeping the drivers you picked to compare.
**A countdown on upcoming weekends.** Each card says how long until its next session, so the schedule answers the question without being opened.

**Android update notice.** With no Google Play listing, a new build used to reach you only if you saw the post in the Telegram channel. The app now checks for one on launch and offers the download, and Settings has a "Check for updates" row. It never interrupts a launch: if the check fails, nothing happens.
Sepang joins the circuit outlines drawn on the schedule cards.
**Race chat marks where you left off.** Coming back to the room, a "New messages" line sits above the first message you have not seen yet.

**A race countdown on the lock screen and the watch face.** Days to the next Grand Prix, then hours on the last day, in three lock screen sizes and as an Apple Watch complication. Once a race is over it moves on to the next round by itself, without opening the app.
**Season progress widget.** One dot for every round, coloured by the team that won it, with the next circuit underneath — on the iPhone home screen and on Android.
Changed: **Race chat reads like a conversation.** Other people's messages sit in bubbles beside their team colour, and the room header is one compact line with the full race name instead of a tall blue block.
The share button has a fill and the share symbol of your platform, so in the light theme it no longer looks switched off.
The session results sheet says which session it is showing. Opening qualifying and the race in turn, only the time column told them apart.
The standings screens name the table and the season they are showing.

Android builds are published to a permanent address with a signed APK, a checksum and full release notes, and are listed at <https://p1anb.vercel.app/download>. The Telegram channel is where releases are announced rather than where the file lives.

Opening and closing a standings card is one movement rather than three: the card, its border, the arrow and the points block travel together, in the same time as before. Race weekend cards on the schedule open and close the same way.
The schedule opens with the next race weekend unfolded, not only during race week.

**The chat tab between weekends says when to come back.** It shows the day and time the room opens over the outline of the next circuit, with a live countdown only in the last two days, and the race by its short name instead of the full sponsored title. "Remind me" sits right under it, your profile card opens account settings, and the previous weekend's room is one tap away to read.

**The chat account screen shows what you have done in the chat.** Your profile card counts your messages, the race weekends you posted in and the reactions other people left, and has its own Edit button. The rest is two short groups: notifications and blocked users (with the count visible before you open it), then how you signed in, sign out and account deletion.
An open standings card no longer shows the arrow: it fades out and the points total takes its place.
The race week card offers the race dashboard as soon as the race data is in, instead of waiting for the weekend to move to Past at midnight.
Fixed: The share sheet no longer grows past the top of the screen on a long card, such as a race classification, and the Share button stays on screen: the preview scrolls beneath it.

A screen opened from outside the app — a link, or a chat mention tapped while the app was closed — had a back button that did nothing, and no way out short of closing the app. It now goes back to the schedule.

Tapping a mention notification while the app was closed opened the app but not the conversation it pointed at. It now lands on the message it named, and a second mention in a room you already have open scrolls to it too.

Opening driver cards in quick succession could show one driver's last five races under another driver's name, most often on Android. Results and team line-ups no longer belong to the row they were loaded in.
A card whose results failed to load said it had no results and never tried again. It now says the load failed and retries when tapped.
The race chat header showed LIVE for the whole weekend, even hours before a session. It now shows only while one is running.
An empty strip the height of the tab bar sat between the last chat message and the input field.

**The Apple Watch app gets its data from your iPhone.** It could never read what the phone saved and fetched the schedule over the network on every launch instead; it now also follows the accent colour you picked.

Added: **Race chat.** A live room for every race weekend, open to read without an account and to post once you sign in with Apple or Google. Replies, reactions, mentions, and a pinned banner for the message you were sent to. Every room message can push to your device, and you decide whether it does.
**Notification settings.** A screen of its own: session reminders and the news topic can each be switched off without touching system settings.
**Android home screen widgets**, including a 2×2 layout and a tall one.
**Report, block and delete.** Any message can be reported and any user blocked from a long press, and a chat account can be deleted in full from Settings without contacting anyone.
Championship points are topped up from OpenF1 when f1api has not published a round yet, so standings stop lagging a race behind.
Changed: Session results, session end times and the starting grid now come from OpenF1, with f1api kept as the fallback.
The settings screen was rebuilt on shared sections and rows, and the theme was resynced with the Figma source.
Fixed: Safety-car bands on the race dashboard were drawn wrong whenever a race was red-flagged: one band could run from lap 3 to the chequered flag. Full and virtual safety cars are also tracked separately now, and a 2026-season rename of the virtual safety car no longer files it as a full one.
A race stays in its race-week state until the race day is actually over.
Push tokens and notification payloads no longer reach release-build logs.
